creator: Alexander Terp
description:
A `del` during a `for` loop over a map silently visits one key twice and skips
another. Deleting the key the loop is currently on takes the interpreter down.

```rad
m = {"a": 1, "b": 2, "c": 3}
for k, v in m:
    if k == "a":
        del m["b"]
    print(k, v)
```

```
a 1
c 3
c 3
```

Deleting the current key instead (`del m[k]`):

```
error[RAD20042]: This is a bug in Rad. Please report it at: ...
  Panic: Bug! Unhandled Rad type in Type: '<nil>'
  core/interpreter.go:1498
```

`Keys()` in `core/type_map.go` returns `m.keys` itself rather than a copy, so
`Delete`'s in-place `append` shifts the remaining keys out from under the loop
ranging over them.

`docs/type_system.md` already describes the behavior we want - "A for-loop over
a map iterates a snapshot of the keys taken before the first iteration" - so the
doc is right and the code doesn't honor it. Handing back a copy would make both
true; worth checking `Keys()`'s other callers before assuming that's free
everywhere.

Lists are deliberately different - mutation there is visible to a running loop,
matching Python - and that half of the doc is accurate. Whatever lands here,
`docs/type_system.md` needs to match it.

Found during the v0.12.0 docs review, on v0.12.0.
title: Deleting during map iteration skips a key and can panic
